initiatives.title: Deprecate REPLACE TABLE in REST Catalog
initiatives.summary: Discussion on whether to deprecate Iceberg's REPLACE TABLE operation due to its complexity and confusing semantics. Participants argue that REPLACE TABLE's truncate-and-maintain-state behavior adds unnecessary complexity compared to explicit DROP+CREATE or TRUNCATE+INSERT operations, and that it creates unsafe metadata state transitions that are difficult to reason about.
key_points: REPLACE TABLE semantics are confusing to users who expect simple drop+create behavior
Current implementation retains permissions, history, and schema IDs across unrelated table states, creating safety issues
Metadata state transitions (properties, location, stats) are not properly versioned and hard to reason about
Explicit operations (TRUNCATE+INSERT or DROP+CREATE) provide clearer semantics and better control over permissions and history
Most database systems like PostgreSQL and Oracle don't offer REPLACE TABLE, requiring explicit operations instead

initiatives.title: Support set(metadata) on TableOperations interface
initiatives.summary: Proposal to add a new set(metadata) method to TableOperations for unconditionally setting table metadata, addressing limitations of the current commit API when implementing overwrite registration for external tables. The new method would bypass base state checks and avoid unnecessary metadata file creation and deletion.
key_points: Current commit(base, new) API assumes base metadata matches current state, unsuitable for overwrite registration
Commit always writes new metadata.json files, problematic when reusing user-provided metadata
Failed commits attempt to delete metadata files, inappropriate when files originated elsewhere
Drop-and-recreate alternative risks leaving table in invalid intermediate state on failure
Proposed set(metadata) would atomically replace metadata without base state validation

initiatives.title: FileIO Resource Management Issue in Spark
initiatives.summary: PR #12868 addresses a critical issue where Spark's broadcast variable cleanup calls FileIO.close() and unintentionally shuts down shared resources like HTTP connection pools, breaking Iceberg queries on Spark. The issue is particularly acute with S3FileIO using ApacheHttpClient where all instances share the same connection pool. Community review is requested on the proposed solution and whether a more explicit resource ownership model is needed.
key_points: Spark broadcasts FileIO instances to executors and calls close() during cleanup, terminating shared resources
S3FileIO with ApacheHttpClient is particularly affected as all instances share a single connection pool
The core problem involves broader resource lifecycle management within FileIO
Solution impacts many production Iceberg users on Spark

initiatives.summary: Discussion about orphaned Puffin statistics files remaining in storage after dropTableData() calls. The issue occurs because updateStatistics() creates new metadata versions without deleting old stat files, and dropTableData() only removes files referenced in the latest metadata. The author proposes three alternative solutions with different trade-offs in performance and complexity.

Seeks community feedback on proposed approach

initiatives.title: Evaluate Immutables library adoption for Iceberg
initiatives.summary: Proposal to introduce the Immutables library (Apache License 2.0) to Iceberg via annotation processing for generating immutable, type-safe, and thread-safe value classes. The library would reduce boilerplate code, provide automatic builder generation, and enable JSON serialization/deserialization support, particularly beneficial for the REST-based Catalog implementation.
key_points: Immutables library generates immutable implementation classes from annotated abstract value classes
Reduces boilerplate code for getters, setters, hashCode, equals, and toString methods
Provides automatic builder classes and JSON serialization/deserialization support
Ensures thread-safety and null-safety with mandatory attribute validation
Proof-of-concept implementations shown in TableIdentifier/Namespace and TableMetadata PRs

initiatives.title: Reference names in TableIdentifier for snapshot tagging
initiatives.summary: Discussion on how to handle reference names (branches/tags) in TableIdentifier to distinguish between tables on different branches, such as namespace.tbl (default branch) versus namespace.tbl@dev (specific branch). The proposal also addresses cache invalidation challenges when multiple branch references exist for the same table.
key_points: Need to distinguish table references by branch/tag in TableIdentifier syntax
Cache invalidation complexity with multiple branch references for same table
Design considerations documented in shared Google Doc

initiatives.title: Forward compatibility and snapshot ID inheritance strategy
initiatives.summary: Discussion on how to handle snapshot ID inheritance as an optional field without breaking forward compatibility with older readers. Proposes using feature flags to allow early adoption of breaking changes within a format version, rather than immediately bumping the format version.
key_points: Snapshot ID inheritance makes the snapshot ID field optional in manifests, which breaks forward compatibility with older readers
Format version bump would break compatibility for all tables, even those not using appended manifests
Proposed solution: use feature flags to opt tables into breaking changes, allowing gradual adoption and format v2 to standardize the feature
This strategy enables releasing format features early behind flags before they become mandatory in a new format version
